name: MCP41010-I_SN
title: MCP41XXX/42XXX: single and dual 256-position digital potentiometers, 10 kΩ, 50 kΩ or 100 kΩ, SPI
summary: A family of 8-bit (256-tap) linear digital potentiometers set over SPI, in 10 kΩ, 50 kΩ and 100 kΩ end-to-end values. The MCP41XXX has one potentiometer in an 8-pin package; the MCP42XXX has two in a 14-pin package and adds a serial output for daisy chains plus hardware reset and shutdown pins. The parts run from one 2.7 V to 5.5 V supply, draw under 1 µA when idle, start at mid-scale (80h), and a shutdown opens terminal A and ties the wiper to B. MCP41010-I/SN is the single 10 kΩ part, -40 °C to +85 °C, in the 8-lead 150 mil SOIC.

pins.name: RS
pins.function: Reset, active low, Schmitt trigger with an active pull-up. Held low for 150 ns or more it sets every potentiometer to 80h. Keep it high while CS is low; do not let it float.

pins.name: SHDN
pins.function: Shutdown, active low, Schmitt trigger with an active pull-up. Low opens terminal A and joins W to B on every potentiometer; register contents are kept. Keep it high while CS is low; do not let it float.

pins.name: SO
pins.function: Serial data out from the end of the 16-bit shift register, for daisy chains; changes on SCK falling edges. Push-pull, never high-impedance: it drives low whenever CS is high.

operation.text: Each potentiometer is a resistor string with 256 tap positions and an 8-bit data register choosing the wiper's tap. The SPI port fills a 16-bit shift register whose data byte is moved into the data registers. Resistance from the wiper to either end changes linearly with the code; 00h sits at B.
A power-on reset sets every data register to mid-scale, 80h. Powering up with SHDN low gives shutdown mode with the registers at 80h.

CS goes low, then a command byte and a data byte (16 clocks) are shifted in MSB first. Data enter on rising SCK edges and leave SO on falling edges. The command runs when CS rises. The part counts rising edges while CS is low; anything other than a multiple of 16 aborts the command. After a command the shift register refills with zeros.
Mode 0,0 (clock idles low) and mode 1,1 (clock idles high) both work; in each, input is sampled on the rising edge and SO changes after the falling edge.

C1 C0 = 01 writes the data byte to the potentiometers whose select bits P1, P0 are 1. C1 C0 = 10 shuts down the selected potentiometers; its data byte must still be sent but is ignored. 00 and 11 are no-operation, useful in a chain.

A shut-down potentiometer has terminal A open and B joined to W. It stays so until a valid write to it, taking effect on the CS rising edge if SHDN is high (with SHDN low the register still updates but the part stays shut down), or until power is cycled. On the MCP42XXX a CS low pulse followed by an RS low pulse of 150 ns or more (SHDN high, CS high) or by a rising edge on SHDN after at least 100 ns low (CS high) also ends it; sharing one SHDN or RS line, the CS pulse picks which device wakes.

SHDN low shuts down every potentiometer regardless of software state, leaving the registers unchanged. Registers can still be written and RS still resets them while SHDN is low; new values apply when SHDN rises. SHDN must not fall while CS is low: that state is invalid and leaves the outcome undefined.

An RS pulse of 150 ns or longer, taken while CS is high, sets every data latch to 80h, whatever SCK, SI and SHDN are doing. With SHDN low the registers reset but the outputs stay shut down until SHDN rises. Pulling RS down during a CS-low transfer is not allowed and gives undefined results. RS and SHDN have active pull-ups drawing next to nothing at either logic level, and must not float.

SO of one device feeds SI of the next; all share CS and SCK. SO carries the shift register's output; because each register is cleared to zeros after a command, the first 16 bits a device passes on are zeros, i.e. a NOP to the next one. Only the devices up to the farthest one needing a command must be clocked: 16 clocks per device, all executing together when CS rises. An MCP41XXX, having no SO, can only be the last device. The SO delay limits the chain clock to about 5.8 MHz.

Used as a two-terminal variable resistor, the unused end is tied to the wiper; A and B may be swapped. At code 00h only the wiper resistance remains, so the current must stay at or below 1 mA. Resistance has a positive tempco; codes 00h to 0Fh vary most with temperature because of the wiper, the rest follow the 800 ppm/°C typ of RAB. Dual parts match A-to-B resistance within 1 % between channels; part to part it may differ by up to 30 %.

With all three terminals on separate nodes the wiper gives a voltage proportional to the one across A and B; A and B may be swapped. Tempco is set by resistor ratio, typically 1 ppm/°C at 80h. At low codes the wiper's tempco dominates; above them about 70 % of codes typically stay under 5 ppm/°C and 30 % under 1 ppm/°C.

For linear behaviour the analog signals on the potentiometer and the op-amp's inputs and output must lie between VSS and VDD. An inverting single-supply stage needs a reference or virtual ground at the non-inverting input.

In the inverting and differential amplifiers gain rises as the wiper moves toward A and falls toward B, roughly logarithmically around code 128; near either end each step changes gain by large amounts because RA and RB are badly mismatched. Gains of 0.1 to 10 V/V are recommended. The differential amplifier needs both potentiometers at one code and gains from the channel matching of a dual part and the low divider tempco.

A divider-mode potentiometer between two fixed resistors and a buffer gives an output linear in code; R1 and R2 set the step size and the end voltages, and can be chosen to avoid the low codes where wiper resistance hurts tempco most.

Bypass VDD with 0.1 µF as near the pin as possible. Keep digital and analog traces apart, with no traces under the part or its bypass capacitor, and route clock and other fast lines well away from analog ones. An analog ground plane keeps all parts at one ground potential.

circuits.title: Connection to a microcontroller with bypassing
circuits.description: A microcontroller drives the potentiometer's CS, SCK and SI. Each chip has its own 0.1 µF capacitor from VDD to ground, placed at its supply pin. The three potentiometer terminals go on to the circuit being adjusted.

circuits.title: Rheostat (two-terminal) connection
circuits.description: Joining terminal A to the wiper makes the part one variable resistor between two nodes, set by the code: least at 00h, most at FFh.

circuits.title: Potentiometer (voltage divider) connection
circuits.description: Terminal A takes the input voltage V1 and terminal B is grounded; the wiper output V2 is a fraction of V1 set by the code.

circuits.title: Programmable inverting gain amplifier, single supply
circuits.description: The input reaches the op-amp's inverting input through the A-to-wiper half of the potentiometer, and the wiper-to-B half returns the output to it, so the code sets the gain RB/RA. The non-inverting input sits at a reference voltage. The op-amp's input current is negligible, so wiper resistance does not enter the gain.

circuits.title: Programmable non-inverting gain amplifier, single supply
circuits.description: The op-amp takes the input on its non-inverting input. The potentiometer is its feedback divider: B to the output, A to ground, wiper to the inverting input, giving a gain of 1 + RB/RA set by the code.

circuits.title: Programmable differential amplifier, single supply
circuits.description: The two halves of an MCP42010 work as a difference amplifier around an MCP601. SIG- (VB) enters potentiometer 0 at A, whose wiper drives the inverting input and whose B end is the output feedback. SIG+ (VA) enters potentiometer 1 at A, whose B end is at VREF and whose wiper drives the non-inverting input. Set to one common code, they give an output of (VA - VB) × RB/RA.
notes: The two potentiometers must be of equal value.
Misprint: the op-amp polarity marks are reversed against the -IN and +IN labels; the upper input is -IN, the lower +IN.

circuits.title: Programmable offset trim (voltage reference)
circuits.description: R1 from VDD to A and R2 from B to VSS put the potentiometer's span inside a chosen window; the wiper, filtered by 0.1 µF to ground, is buffered by an MCP606 follower. The output steps linearly with code, and R1, R2 set the step size and the end voltages.
notes: R1 and R2 have no given values; they are chosen for the output range and resolution.

circuits.title: Three devices in a daisy chain
circuits.description: One chip select and one clock from the microcontroller reach all three devices. The microcontroller's SO feeds device 1's SI, device 1's SO feeds device 2, and device 2's SO feeds device 3. Device 3, the last, may be a single MCP41XXX since its SO is not used. 48 clocks load all three, and they act together when CS rises.
notes: Example load: device 1 XX10XX11 11001100, device 2 XX01XX10 11110000, device 3 XX10XX00 10101010, sent device 3 first.
